chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who sets aside something for his children while they are young, then it occurs to him to include others among his children with them, he said: 'There is no harm in that.'

key_terms.لاَ بَأْسَ: there is no harm / it is permissible
key_terms.يَبْدُو لَهُ: it occurs to him / it becomes apparent to him

ai.seo_question: Can a father change his mind about which children receive a specific gift or allocation from his wealth?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadi’ (AS) to clarify that a father’s gift (*hibah*) to minor children remains revocable or modifiable until the children reach maturity or the gift is formally completed. This permissibility (*la ba'sa*) underscores the father’s discretion in managing family wealth during the children's minority, distinguishing it from fixed inheritance shares that are distributed after death. The ruling highlights the flexibility in Islamic family law regarding interim wealth allocation before the finalization of property rights.
